video.title: The summer Math fell to the machines...

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Cold open: developers are doing fine despite AI doom, 'sadly our mathematician friends may not be so lucky' -- in three weeks AI killed more open math problems than humans did in a decade; an 87-year-old conjecture disproven during the World Cup final, a 30-year-old one to four prompts (34.0). Continuing to Terence Tao warning of a crisis in the foundations of mathematics (52.3) also works as a weightier kicker; the end range spans both, shorter preferred. Opening at 12.5 ('Sadly, our mathematician friends...') is acceptable but loses the contrast.

A mathematician posts a counterexample disproving the Jacobian conjecture (soccer/air-conditioning joke up front), a plain-English explanation of the conjecture, why it sat on Smale's list since 1939 -- payoff: 'until [he] did last month with some help from Fable' (144.6, ending at the clause's comma before the next example).

Anthropic's model made progress on the Riemann hypothesis (167 years old, million-dollar bounty); the best part: it wasn't a mathematician but the creator of Bun on his jog, 650 wrong ideas, then 60 sub-agents, 31M tokens, and the fraction provably satisfying the hypothesis went from 41% to 67% (307.0). The validation line (313.9) is acceptable. 'fired back' nods to the OpenAI section but reads as rivalry without it; starting at 'Anthropic' (244.8) drops the 'So just last week' run-up.

also_ok.why: 30-year-old graph-theory conjecture explained as delivery routing; a researcher told GPT to 'make a breakthrough' and it answered with a seven-node, nine-edge counterexample. Good surprising fact, but the only clean opening is 'just two days later it happened again', which points back -- acceptable, not insisted on.

OpenAI 'got in on the bullying': its next model solved ten open problems with Lean certificates; the ball-packing bound hadn't moved since 1978 until now, with a 'some of you have thought about balls a lot' joke. Opens on a run-up and is mostly a list; acceptable.

negatives.why: Intro: 'In today's video...', date, Code Report.

Timeline recap: IMO results, the Erdős unit-distance disproof with what sounds like a played quote ('Couldn't believe it... trouble sleeping'), the Leiden Declaration 'politely ignored' joke -- lively but a chronology.
'It's not just the pros': a PhD student's six Erdős problems and an amateur -- truncated list items with no payoff.
